title: Ragi Carrot & Banana Pancakes
summary: Small soft pancakes of banana, grated carrot and ragi flour. No sugar, one bowl, 15 minutes.

substitutes.name: oat flour
substitutes.note: use certified gluten-free oats if needed

substitutes.name: flax egg
substitutes.note: ground flaxseed mixed with 3 tbsp water, rested 5 minutes; egg-free

ingredients.name: milk
ingredients.note: only if the batter is too stiff

steps.text: Mash {banana} in a bowl with a fork until smooth.
Add {carrot}, {flour}, {egg}, {baking-powder} and {spice}, and mix until no dry flour is left.
steps.tip: Scrape the dry flour off the sides of the bowl into the batter.

steps.text: Check the batter: it should drop slowly from a spoon. If it is stiff, stir in {milk}.
Heat a nonstick pan on medium-low heat and wipe it with {butter}.
Drop 1 tablespoon of batter per pancake into the pan and press each one to about 1 cm thick.
steps.tip: Thick batter does not spread on its own.

steps.text: Cook until the edges look dry, then flip and cook the other side.
steps.tip: Ragi batter is already dark, so judge by the edges, not the colour. Break the first one open to check the middle is cooked.

steps.text: Cool a little, then serve whole or in strips.

toddlerTips: No sugar needed: the banana sweetens it. No honey under 12 months.
For 2-year-olds, grate the carrot on the medium side and serve with plain yogurt to dip and halved blueberries.
Toddlers can mash the banana and stir the batter. Keep them away from the pan.
Fridge up to 3 days. To freeze, lay them on a tray, then move to a bag. Reheat in a pan or microwave.
Tested at home with ragi flour in place of spelt: the banana, egg and carrot gave enough liquid, so no milk was needed.
